QuestionStmt.S:
A random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
X & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\
\hline
P(X) & k & 2k & 4k & 2k & k \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

then the value of $P(1 \leq X < 4 \mid X \leq 2) =$

Solution.S:
First, find $k$ using $\sum P(X) = 1$:

$$k + 2k + 4k + 2k + k = 10k = 1 \quad \Rightarrow \quad k = \frac{1}{10}$$

Now,

$$P(1 \leq X < 4) = P(X=1) + P(X=2) + P(X=3) = 2k + 4k + 2k = 8k = \frac{8}{10} = \frac{4}{5}$$

$$P(X \leq 2) = P(X=0) + P(X=1) + P(X=2) = k + 2k + 4k = 7k = \frac{7}{10}$$

Conditional probability:

$$P(1 \leq X < 4 \mid X \leq 2) = \frac{P(1 \leq X < 4 \text{ and } X \leq 2)}{P(X \leq 2)}$$

The intersection $\{1 \leq X < 4\} \cap \{X \leq 2\} = \{1, 2\}$.

$$P(1 \leq X < 4 \text{ and } X \leq 2) = P(X=1) + P(X=2) = 2k + 4k = 6k = \frac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}$$

Thus,

$$\frac{3/5}{7/10} = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{10}{7} = \frac{6}{7}$$

Hence the correct option is B: $\frac{6}{7}$.
